_doc: The Arduino CNC shield V3, Protoneer's design, mostly sold as clones. Figures are community until measured: they come from a clone maker's guide and comparisons of the boards, because Protoneer's own pages could not be reached. The revision matters: V3.00 and V3.51 wire the Z limit and spindle pins differently, so read the rule for limit_pin_z. Board in the x-y plane.
name: cnc-shield-v3

step_pin_x.rule: X step pin on the Uno

dir_pin_x.rule: X direction pin on the Uno

step_pin_y.rule: Y step pin on the Uno

dir_pin_y.rule: Y direction pin on the Uno

step_pin_z.rule: Z step pin on the Uno

dir_pin_z.rule: Z direction pin on the Uno

enable_pin.rule: Enables every driver; active low, shared by all axes

limit_pin_x.rule: X limit switches, both ends share this pin

limit_pin_y.rule: Y limit switches, both ends share this pin

limit_pin_z.rule: Z limit as printed on V3.00 boards and in Grbl 0.8. Grbl 0.9 and later with variable spindle (the default) wants Z limit on D12 and the spindle on D11, so on those firmwares wire Z limit to the board's spindle-enable pin: V3.51 boards already swap them
limit_pin_z.source: CNC shield V3 clones and Protoneer boards compared, https://hackaday.io/project/176110/log/190386

a_axis.value: clone of X, Y or Z, or D12 and D13 for a free fourth axis
a_axis.rule: The A socket has no pins of its own: two jumper pairs beside it copy the step and direction of X, Y or Z, or route them to D12 and D13 when firmware drives A independently (D12 and D13 are also the spindle pins, so they can't do both)

spindle_pins.value: D12 enable, D13 direction (V3.00); D11 enable/PWM, D13 direction (V3.51)
spindle_pins.rule: The spindle control pins, by board revision
spindle_pins.source: CNC shield V3 clones and Protoneer boards compared, https://hackaday.io/project/176110/log/190386

other_pins.value: A0 abort, A1 hold, A2 resume, A3 coolant

microstep_jumpers.value: M0 M1 M2: none full; M0 half; M1 quarter; M0 M1 eighth; M0 M1 M2 sixteenth (A4988) or 1/32 (DRV8825); M2 only 1/16 (DRV8825)
microstep_jumpers.rule: A jumper on a position pulls that driver's microstep pin high. One set of three under each driver socket

motor_voltage_min.rule: Least motor supply into the screw terminals

motor_voltage_max.rule: Most motor supply into the screw terminals, as sold. An A4988 is only good for 35 V: use a DRV8825 near this

body_width.rule: Board length, about; the Uno footprint

body_depth.rule: Board width, about; the Uno footprint

pinout.value: D2 Xstep D3 Ystep D4 Zstep D5 Xdir D6 Ydir D7 Zdir D8 enable D9 Xlimit D10 Ylimit D11 Zlimit(V3.00) D12 spindle(V3.00) D13 spindle dir
pinout.rule: The Uno pins the shield uses; see the rules for each pin
